text:
rachel: Hi team, first week here. Trying to build runtime from source on WSL2 (Win11 host) and the build dies with `g++: internal compiler error: Killed (program cc1plus)` during the big linking step. Also seeing `usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcudart` even though I installed CUDA via the toolkit installer. Any quick tips?

tom: welcome! two things to check quickly: WSL2 default VM memory/swap is tiny which often kills big C++ builds. What's `wsl -l -v` and how much memory are you giving it?

rachel: wsl -l -v -> Ubuntu-22.04 running. I didn't tweak memory. I tried `make -j$(nproc)` which is 8.

jess: that's likely the OOM. Reduce parallelism: `JOBS=2 make` or `make -j2`. Or increase WSL memory by creating a `.wslconfig` in your Windows user folder with something like:

```
[wsl2]
memory=8GB   # or 16GB
swap=4GB
processors=4
```

then `wsl --shutdown` and restart.

rachel: ok lowering jobs helped the cc1plus crash go away. Still have `cannot find -lcudart`. I installed CUDA toolkit on Windows and set `PATH` in /etc/profile? Not sure if WSL picks that up.

tom: for CUDA-on-WSL you need the Windows NVIDIA driver that supports WSL + the Linux toolkit inside WSL. Check `nvidia-smi` inside WSL (should show GPUs). Also ensure the Linux CUDA install created `/usr/local/cuda` symlink and that `/usr/local/cuda/lib64` is in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` or run `sudo ldconfig` after adding `/usr/local/cuda/lib64` to `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/cuda.conf`.

rachel: `nvidia-smi` inside WSL returns GPU info, so driver is exposed. There's a `/usr/local/cuda-12.2` dir but no `/usr/local/cuda` symlink.

jess: create the symlink: `sudo ln -s /usr/local/cuda-12.2 /usr/local/cuda` then `sudo ldconfig`. Also verify `ls /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so*`. If missing, the toolkit install may have been partial; try reinstalling the Linux toolkit inside WSL.

buildbot: FYI: our CI uses `--with-cuda=/usr/local/cuda-12.2` in the build flags to avoid ambiguous symlinks.

rachel: did the symlink + ldconfig. `ldconfig` shows `/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12` present. Re-ran make and now failing on undefined references during linking: `undefined reference to __cudaRegisterFatBinary` etc.

tom: those undefined refs usually mean the nvcc-produced obj files weren't linked with `-lcudart_static` or the host compiler flags didn't include `-Wl,--no-as-needed -lcudart`. How are you invoking the build?

rachel: just `JOBS=2 make` using the top-level Makefile.

jess: check `config.mk` or `local.mk` in repo; we have a flag `USE_CUDA=1` and `CUDA_LIBS=-L/usr/local/cuda/lib64 -lcudart`. If your env had `CUDA_HOME` unset, the auto-detect might skip adding correct flags. Run `export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda` then `make clean && make JOBS=2`.

rachel: export fixed it! build finished (took quite a while). Thanks folks. A couple of onboarding notes that might help future WSL users: add a short doc in onboarding about WSL memory (.wslconfig), symlink/LD_LIBRARY pitfalls, and recommending the pre-baked dev VM if they don't want to juggle Windows toolchains. Happy to draft a snippet.

jess: please do! PR that into `docs/onboarding-devbox.md` and ping me for review. Nice first-week win :tada:

infra-bot: onboarding-wsl: https://intra.redwood/dev-onboard/wsl-cuda has an existing checklist (memory, driver, `CUDA_HOME`, ldconfig). If you're drafting a PR, link to that checklist.

rachel: will do, thanks everyone :)
